sources.overlap: Section2.1.1 models H~Hypergeom(N,K,n), then Y|H=Bin(H,Se)+Bin(n-H,1-Sp), integrating over latent sample positives and inverting exact probability calculations. Sp=1 gives precisely the proposed hypergeometric/binomial detection convolution.

sources.title: Exact Finite-Population Sequential Auditing for Selective Release from Model-Proposed Candidate Sets
sources.verified_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract in previous evidence file; direct fulltext unavailable.
sources.overlap: Frozen candidate/audit plans, finite-population release/full-review decisions and exact operating-characteristic calculations.
sources.relevance: Selective-release policy and exact enumeration are established statistical components.

candidate_model.audit_population: All 64 claims after the first-phase repairs, if that pipeline is exercised; prefix claims remain eligible. A standalone component sweep has no first-phase outcome claim.
candidate_model.upper_total: Kplus(k) = max {K in {k,...,N}: F_K(k;q0) > delta}. Search through N, not N-n+k; sampled negatives can be false negatives.
candidate_model.post_repair_upper: max(0, Kplus(k)-k), bounding all remaining stale claims, including sampled false negatives. Subtract verified correctly repaired detections k, not the sample size n or unobserved latent H.
candidate_model.decision: Release only if the post-repair upper count is at most tau; otherwise withhold. Enumerate every k: Kplus(k)-k need not be monotone.
candidate_model.attribution: The convolution and exact inversion specialize Mirzahosseini/Reiczigel (2026) to specificity 1. Monotone-sensitivity coupling is standard stochastic-order reasoning; no new theorem is asserted.
candidate_model.reasoning_check: For true independent q >= q0, detection counts stochastically dominate the q0 model, so inversion at q0 is conservative. Conditioning on the first phase is legitimate only if the fresh audit detection assumptions continue to hold for the remaining population.

assumptions: After any arbitrary first-phase12calls/repairs, freeze all64claim labels and target semantics. Conditional on that history, K is fixed; no unmodeled patch may change another target.

Uniformly sample24distinct claimIDs from all64, independently of hidden residual labels and the audit-stage detection noise. Prefix claims remain eligible because first-phase negatives may be false negatives.

For each sampled stale claim, audit detection is fresh, conditionally independent across claims and independent of first-phase detection given frozen state; its probability is at least knownq0. A merely average historical sensitivity is insufficient.
False positives are absent, or every reported positive is independently confirmed before being counted as a repaired stale claim. False-positive labels cannot simply be subtracted fromK.
Every counted detected stale claim is correctly repaired and no repair introduces a new defect. Numeric correctness of an ideal patch is a separate assumption from detection.
Oneprespecified audit look and a frozenq0,delta,tolerance. Failure means withhold; no noisy fullscan is silently treated as perfect settlement.
Guarantee is per frozen batch over audit sampling and independent detection randomization, not conditional-on-release95percent correctness, global corpus coverage or real-world truth.
calibration_cautions: An independent lower confidence bound q0 can consume a calibration error budget eta. Under a justified shared detector model, a union-bound composition has total error at most eta + delta. Account for both uncertainties explicitly.

An iid calibration mean does not establish a per-claim or per-family sensitivity lower bound. Shift, hard residuals selected by the first phase, shared blind spots and deterministic validators can invalidate transfer.
Independent heterogeneous sensitivities qi >= q0 admit stochastic domination. Marginal sensitivities without independence do not justify binomial thinning.
Consensus, repeated seeds, different provider names and calibrated self-confidence do not establish independent false negatives.
With false positives, the general likelihood includes Bin(n-H,FPR). Subtracting all reported positives from the stale count is unsafe unless positive repairs are confirmed and correct.
A full scan with a fallible judge can still leave false negatives. Withholding, exact external validation or a separately modeled settlement procedure is required.

exact_planning_calculations.label: Deterministic prospective design calculations, not held-out model outcomes.
exact_planning_calculations.arithmetic: Python standard-library Fraction and math.comb, enumerating every K from 0 through 64 and k from 0 through 24 using the stated CDF.
exact_planning_calculations.interpretation: At this fixed budget and tolerance, q0=.8 or .6 admits no passing audit count. Safety may mean 100% withholding; do not tune the tolerance after inspecting results.

counterexamples.name: Naive perfect-label gate with independent false negatives
counterexamples.release_event: Y=0: naive Kplus(0)=6 passes, but K-Y=7 exceeds tau=6.
counterexamples.meaning: For this fixed batch, the naive gate exceeds 5% unconditional unsafe-release probability.

counterexamples.name: Marginal sensitivity does not replace independence
counterexamples.noise_model: One fresh shared Bernoulli switch Z with P(Z=1)=.9; every sampled stale claim is detected exactly when Z=1.
counterexamples.meaning: The independence-based gate can release 64 stale claims with probability 10%, despite marginal detection sensitivity .9 for each claim. This violates an assumption, not the conditional probability argument.

matched_arms: No-certification diagnostic: first phase and the same audit sample; report residual counts without calling the outcome certified release.
Naive q1 gate: identical sample and detections, incorrectly assuming perfect labels; an intentionally misspecified comparator.
Known-q0 noise-aware gate: identical sample and detections, one prespecified look, otherwise withhold.
Perfect-detector q1 oracle: an explicit quality ceiling, not a matched real-judge arm.
recommended_frozen_evaluation.matched_randomness: Share the first-phase history, audit sample and actual detector realization across the first three arms; only bound interpretation differs.
primary_exact_checks: Enumerate all K and feasible Y, checking maximum bound undercoverage and unsafe-release probability on a fixed rational sensitivity grid.
Verify q0=1 reduces to the ordinary hypergeometric bound and q0=0 gives a vacuous total count bound.
A census n=N with q<1 can retain stale claims. Do not treat it as perfect validation.
Compute gate pass probability by summing all passing Y states; residual bound Kplus(Y)-Y can be nonmonotone.
Underestimated q0 is conservative under the assumed model; an overestimated q0 is an explicit assumption violation.
Keep zero-release designs and withheld batches in their proper denominators.
stress_tests: Independent homogeneous detection with known q.
Shared all-or-none or clustered detector noise.
False-positive flags with and without independent confirmation.
Incorrect repairs or post-audit source changes: explicit assumption violations.
metrics: Unsafe release overall and conditional on release, with distinct denominators.
All-current frequency and residual stale-count distribution.
Detector calls, including revisits, retries and first-phase calls when present.
Distinct inspected claims separately from detector-call counts.
Correct repairs, repair damage and calibration-label cost when applicable.
recommended_frozen_evaluation.scope: First validate exact known-noise operating characteristics, then measure actual judge error structure on independent adjudicated tasks. This does not demonstrate empirical LLM certification by itself.

publication_position: A controlled workspace-specific boundary study can implement existing misclassification-aware audit machinery and expose assumption failures. It establishes neither new statistical theory, first noisy-judge certification, nor production repair capability.
implementation_hazards: False negatives invalidate the perfect-label support restriction K <= N-n+k; inversion must search K through N.
Fresh audit calls may revisit a first-phase claim. Charge every call and separately count distinct claim IDs; a 12+24 call pipeline does not inspect 36 distinct claims when sampling from all 64.
Do not implement release as a single low-count cutoff without checking every state. The independent reviewer found n=N=64,q0=.9,tau=6 passes Y=0..27 and Y=58..64, while intermediate Y can fail.
A standalone N=64 component sweep must not be described as the prior post-discovery N=52 pool or as an executed first-phase pipeline.
Exact arithmetic verifies operating characteristics under a declared detector model. It does not estimate an actual language model sensitivity.
